item.title: Anthropic unveils Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models ahead of IPO
item.description:
If you're about to ask investors for $100 billion, it's a good time to have something new to sell.

Anthropic today launched Claude Fable 5.2 and its unrestricted counterpart, Mythos 5.2, with the company claiming another significant leap in performance at a lower price. The first impression isn't great, as it doesn't look like a big leap forward.

The timing is notable as Anthropic prepares for what could be the largest IPO in history, potentially raising $80 billion to $100 billion at a valuation of as much as $1.75 trillion.

The company says the new models outperform Opus 5.5 on nearly every benchmark it tested, including a win over OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra in agentic coding. Fable 5.2 scored 69.9% on FrontierSWE v2 compared to 65.5% for Astra.

From the PR:

Testers have found that Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 communicate more clearly than past Fable and Mythos models. They generate outputs up to 30% faster than Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, and they’re available at a lower price: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens.

That's about 20% cheaper than the prior benchmarks.

For investors, the price cut might be the most important part of the announcement.

One of the biggest questions surrounding the AI trade is whether the economics ultimately work. There's little doubt about demand but the costs of delivering increasingly powerful models remain enormous.

Anthropic says Fable 5.2 running at High effort can match Opus 5.5 at Max effort on coding tasks at roughly half the cost.

That's a meaningful improvement and it fits with what we've seen throughout the AI boom but it's not some kind of revolution that will get the market frothing for hte IPO.

Anthropic also says Claude now writes more than 90% of the code merged into its own core codebase. That's the kind of statistic that will feature prominently in an IPO roadshow.

There are also signs that the economics are improving. Compute costs have fallen from 172% of revenue to 57% over the past year. That remains an expensive business, but it's a dramatic improvement and one that suggests there's more to come.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: NZDUSD buyers are starting to take back control after reaching the lowest level since April 2025
item.description:
The dollar gives back gains. The kiwi gets an extra lift.

The NZDUSD fell to its lowest level since April 2025 on Friday, reaching 0.5527 before closing the week at 0.55426. The pair is higher today as the US dollar gives back some of Friday’s gains and New Zealand’s election gives the kiwi an extra lift.

On the US side, hopes for progress in diplomacy with Iran helped push crude oil lower and eased haven demand for the dollar. That reversed part of Friday’s USD rally, which followed the strong US jobs report.

On the New Zealand side, Prime Minister Christopher Luxon’s National-led coalition holds 67 of 131 seats in the preliminary count, one seat above the majority threshold. That gives the incumbents a path to stay in power and reduces the near-term odds that an employment objective will be restored alongside the RBNZ’s inflation objective. Markets could read such a change as dovish. About 400,000 special votes are still outstanding, with final results due November 27.

Buyers reclaim the old floor and defend the 100-hour moving average.

On the hourly chart, the first step was a move back above the old floor near 0.55791. That opened the door to the 100-hour moving average at 0.5599. Buyers pushed through that level and tested the 200-hour moving average at 0.56114 before the price rotated lower.

The important part was what happened on the pullback. Buyers leaned against the 100-hour moving average and pushed the price back up to its highest level since Thursday. That puts the next swing area at 0.5625 to 0.5633 in focus.

What next for traders?

A move through 0.5633 would have traders looking toward last week’s high near 0.5657. Above that, the 38.2% retracement of the move down from the August high comes in at 0.57026.

The trading rule is simple. As long as the price holds above the 100-hour moving average at 0.5599, the buyers can stay in the game and work through those targets one at a time. A move back below that average would weaken the rebound and put the old floor near 0.55791 back in play.

In the video above, I walk through the rebound on the hourly chart, show why 0.5599 is the barometer for buyers, and lay out the levels they need to clear to extend the move.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: USDCAD trades back near unchanged as buyers return
item.description:
Recall that USDCAD moved sharply higher on Friday after a stronger US jobs report and a weaker Canadian jobs report. The contrast favored the US dollar, and the price action followed. Buyers took the pair above its 100-period moving average on the 4-hour chart, currently at 1.40289, and its 100-day moving average at 1.40423.

The momentum carried the price through the 1.4068–1.4081 swing area, above the 200-period moving average on the 4-hour chart at 1.41209, and past 1.41297, the low of the next swing area. The move ultimately reached 1.4139.

Sellers had their shot. Buyers stepped back in.

Broad US dollar selling early today gave back some of Friday’s gains. USDCAD slipped below the 38.2% retracement of the move up from the August low at 1.40828 and reached 1.4078, inside the 1.4068–1.4081 swing area. That is where buyers stepped back in. The rebound has taken the price back above the 200-period moving average and up to Friday’s high near 1.4139.

What next for buyers?

A break above 1.4139 would have traders looking toward 1.41532, the high of the swing area that starts at 1.41297. Get and stay above 1.41532, and the next upside target is the 1.4192–1.4204 swing area.

On the downside, the 200-period moving average at 1.41209 is the close risk level. If the price gets back below it and starts to trade comfortably there, it would take some of the steam out of the rebound. Traders would then look back toward the 38.2% retracement at 1.40828 and the swing area just below it.

The trading lesson

Friday’s high tells traders whether buyers can extend the move. The moving average tells them where the rebound starts to lose traction. Keeping those two levels separate gives buyers a nearby level to lean against while they wait to see if the next break can hold.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Morgan Stanley says buy the AI dip, sees $3.4 trillion in hyperscaler spending through 2028
item.description:
Morgan Stanley is urging investors to buy the recent weakness in AI stocks, arguing that the market has overreacted to the US midterm election results and their implications for data center construction.

In a report titled Buy the Drop: AI Investment Opportunities Post the US Midterms, the bank says that the AI investment cycle remains intact, even if political opposition to data centers pushes some construction projects into 2029.

The bank's hyperscaler capex forecasts remain unchanged at $1.6 trillion in 2027 and $1.8 trillion in 2028, although it flags some downside risk to the latter.

Key takeaways:

  • Morgan Stanley expects 20% of US data center projects planned for 2028 to be delayed until 2029, representing 5 gigawatts of capacity.

  • US data center capacity additions are now expected to decline 4% in 2028 before jumping 38% in 2029.

  • Globally, data center additions are forecast to grow 9% in 2028 and 20% in 2029.

  • A shortage of more than 30% in powered data center capacity is expected to persist through 2028.

  • MS favors Amazon, Meta, Alphabet and Microsoft among the hyperscalers.

  • It warns that parts of the AI supply chain could face slower orders, inventory accumulation and margin pressure in 2028.

The concern is largely centered on Texas and Ohio, where newly elected governors could introduce additional requirements for data center construction. Morgan Stanley doesn't expect projects already under construction to be disrupted, leaving its 2027 forecasts unchanged.

Instead, it expects permitting and regulatory delays to push some 2028 projects into 2029. I suspect there were also some bottlenecks developing around power that would have pushed them back in any case.

Further out, MS sees a potential geographical shift in construction, with hyperscalers moving some projects to more accommodating states such as Tennessee and Louisiana. The bank also sees the potential for as much as 20 GW of additional data center development across Asia and EMEA.

Morgan Stanley argues that the delays could ultimately be healthy for the AI investment cycle, smoothing the supply-demand imbalance, supporting lease rates for existing compute capacity and extending the period of investment.

The distinction is between hyperscalers and their suppliers.

The bank is particularly bullish on the largest technology companies, which have the balance sheets, existing infrastructure and technical capabilities to overcome power constraints.

Its preferred names include:

  • Amazon (AMZN), Meta (META) and Alphabet (GOOGL): Overweight, with advantages in scale, capital access and AI development.

  • Microsoft (MSFT): Overweight, with similar advantages.

  • CoreWeave (CRWV): Overweight.

  • Nvidia (NVDA): Overweight, with an important role in improving the amount of AI output generated per watt of power.

All of them are up 2-8% today, with the exception of Nvidia, which is down 6% after the Jensen Huang honeypot allegations. CoreWeave reports on Tuesday and the leader, up 8%.

Morgan Stanley highlights the potential for dramatic efficiency improvements in AI models, including Meta's target of a tenfold increase in compute efficiency in 2027.

The bank argues that advances in model architecture, distillation, training techniques and specialized chips could allow AI applications to scale much faster without corresponding increases in computing requirements.

Meanwhile, the outlook is more complicated for companies supplying the data center construction boom.

If the bottleneck shifts from equipment availability to powered buildings, suppliers could experience reduced pricing power, rising inventories and slowing orders. Morgan Stanley warns that the sector could see a traditional downcycle in 2028, including margin normalization and earnings downgrades, even as underlying AI demand remains strong.

That makes stock selection increasingly important.

Among infrastructure-related opportunities, the bank highlights Equinix (EQIX) and powered-shell providers, including WULF, RIOT, HUT and APLD, which it sees as less exposed to Texas-related risks. It flags CIFR, GLXY and MARA as potentially more vulnerable to construction delays or moratoriums. All the mentioned names are up strongly (4-9%) except Cipher, which is down 2.2%.

The financing outlook also favors established companies. Morgan Stanley expects AI-related debt issuance to rise in 2027, but says new data center developments and neocloud operators will face greater scrutiny from lenders.

The broader message is that the AI buildout isn't ending, but the winners may be changing. The largest hyperscalers could benefit from tighter capacity, better compute efficiency and weaker competition, while some equipment suppliers face a more difficult transition as the construction timeline shifts.

Morgan Stanley sees the recent selloff as an opportunity, but it's clearly not recommending buying every AI-related stock indiscriminately. Looking ahead, eyes are on the Anthropic IPO with a report on Friday saying it will go ahead this month.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: US stocks rebound even as Nvidia slides 4%. What next technically
item.description:
Nvidia shares are down about 4% and trading within $5 of their 2026 low, but the broader US stock indices are pushing higher. The technical question now is which indices can hold above the levels they’ve reclaimed and which still have work to do.

S&P 500 buyers clear 7,507.77

The S&P 500 has moved above the swing level near 7,507.77. That gives buyers a short-term technical edge and a close level to lean against. As long as the index can stay above it, the next target is the swing area between 7,573 and 7,617, with the 100-day moving average just above at 7,619.69.

Getting and staying above both the swing area and the 100-day moving average would strengthen the bullish bias. A move back below 7,507.77 would take some of the momentum out of today’s break.

Nasdaq Composite reclaims its 200-day moving average

The Nasdaq Composite is back above 25,036.33, the 38.2% retracement of the move up from the 2026 low to the 2026 high. It has also pushed above its 200-day moving average at 25,106.70. That moving average is the first barometer for buyers. Hold above it and the rebound has a firmer footing. Fall back below it and 25,036.33 comes back into focus.

Recall that last week’s decline found buyers in the 24,206–24,425 area, where the 50% midpoint and swing support came into play. That was where buyers first stepped in. The test now is whether they can defend the levels they’ve taken back.

Nasdaq 100 leads the rebound with its 200-day still overhead

The Nasdaq 100 fell below both its July low at 27,176.03 and the 50% midpoint of the 2026 range at 27,103.07 last week. Today, it’s the best performer of the three indices, up about 2.75% and reaching a high of 27,774.88 so far.

The first hurdle is the 200-day moving average at 27,994.59. If buyers can get and stay above it, the next target is 28,108.03, the broken 38.2% retracement of the 2026 trading range. Clearing and holding above both levels would give the rebound a more bullish technical bias.

The trading lesson

The Nasdaq 100 has the biggest percentage gain of the three, while the Nasdaq Composite has already reclaimed its 200-day moving average. Those are two different measures of strength. The percentage gain tells you how far an index has bounced. The levels it reclaims and holds tell you where buyers can define their risk and what they need to clear next.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: US September wholesale inventories +0.7% vs +0.6% expected
item.description:
• Prior was +0.5%
  • Wholesale sales +2.8% vs 1.8% prior (revised to +2.0%)

The inventory number is slightly positive for Q3 GDP.

For background, the Census Bureau’s monthly wholesale trade report, formally Monthly Wholesale Trade: Sales and Inventories, is released at 10 am ET about five to six weeks after the reference month ends. It covers merchant wholesalers, the businesses that buy goods from manufacturers and resell them to retailers, other businesses and institutions, excluding manufacturers’ own sales branches and offices.

The headline figure is the monthly change in wholesale inventories. An advance estimate is published about a week or two earlier in the Advance Economic Indicators report, so the full release is largely a revision to a number markets have already seen. It also adds wholesale sales and a detailed breakdown between durable goods, such as machinery, autos and parts, metals, lumber and electrical equipment, and nondurable goods, such as groceries, drugs, chemicals, petroleum and farm products.

The inventory-to-sales ratio shows how many months it would take wholesalers to clear existing stock at the current pace of sales. A rising ratio can signal softening demand or deliberate stockpiling, while a falling ratio suggests lean supply and potential restocking ahead. The figures are in nominal dollars, so price swings, particularly in petroleum products, can move the numbers without any change in physical volume.

The report’s main use is in GDP tracking. Changes in private inventories are one of the most volatile contributors to quarterly growth, and the wholesale figures feed into economists’ and nowcasting models’ estimates of that component.

Wholesale inventories rarely move markets. They’ve drawn more attention in recent years as tariff-driven stockpiling and subsequent drawdowns have created large swings in inventory investment and distorted quarterly GDP.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Crude oil is trading above and below a key technical confluence area. Who will take charge?
item.description:
Crude oil is trading lower today as the market weighs the potential for an end to the war with Iran. In his 60 Minutes interview, Pres. Trump signaled he was reluctant to escalate the conflict. As Adam Button reported, the selling picked up after Al Hadath said Trump asked Iraq’s prime minister to relay proposals to Tehran and help mediate an end to the war. The headlines are taking some of the war premium out of crude oil.

In the video above, I take a look at what the selloff did to crude oil technically. The price broke below three support levels in a span of just 24 cents. Where can sellers now lean against resistance to define their risk? What would the buyers need to do to turn the move lower into a failed break? I walk through both scenarios on the chart.

The politics matter. Republicans lost control of both the House and Senate in the midterms, and the war and higher gasoline prices were part of the backlash. That gives the White House more incentive to find a diplomatic solution. For oil traders, the question is whether those efforts lead to progress on the Strait of Hormuz. Adam also noted that a Qatari official pushed back on a report that Iran had dropped its demand to control the strait and collect transit fees. That helps explain why the price can move quickly in either direction as the headlines cross.

Technically, the move lower took crude oil below three levels.

  • The 100-day moving average at $87.17.

  • The 200-day moving average at $87.10.

  • The 50% midpoint of the move up from the July low at $86.93.

That $86.93 to $87.17 area is the barometer for both buyers and sellers. The sellers made the first move by taking the price below the entire cluster. Can they keep it there? If a bounce stalls below $86.93 and the price turns back down with momentum, the old support starts to act as resistance. That would give sellers more confidence that there is room to run to the downside.

Conversely, if the price moves back into the zone, the sellers’ grip starts to loosen. Get back above $87.17 and stay above it, and the break lower starts to look like a failed break. That could force some sellers to cover and give buyers room to rotate the price higher.

The education. When two moving averages and a retracement level come together, think of them as a zone. The first move through the zone tells you who made the first push. The next test tells you more about who is in control. Here, $86.93 is the level sellers can lean against from below, while $87.17 is the level buyers need to reclaim and hold. That gives both sides a nearby level to define risk while the headlines keep coming.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Brent crude breaks the 200-day moving average in fall to a two-month low
item.description:
Oil is plunging today in a continuation of the move since the US midterms.

The market is sensing that the White House is desperate to find a way out of an unpopular war, hoping to turn the page on a decision that sparked a jump in oil prices and problematic inflation. 

Now that's easier said than done but there is a report that JD Vance will head to the Middle East next week to negotiate directly with Iran. Those sorts of meetings generally only happen when the broad strokes of some kind of agreement are worked out.

Of course, there have been so many false reports about Iran and the sourcing on the Vance report is iffy but there have been a multitude of leaks lately that suggest there is some real progress. And the price action in oil is undeniable.

Brent crude is down $5.18 to $93.10 today and that cuts through the 200-day moving average, a level that held last week.

The drop today puts brent at the lowest since early September.

As you can see, the 200-day hasn't been pivotal in the past two months but the speed of selling down to $93 from $118 is dramatic and meaningful, not only for oil but for the macro picture. 

Partly in response, the S&P 500 is up 1.2% today to 7466. Ultimately, Trump measures himself based on the stock market and the best thing he can do right now to support it is end the war and give the Fed a reason to pause rate hikes. At the moment, the market sees a 81% chance of a December hike and 50 bps of hikes through the coming year.

Obviously oil has moved quickly here that reflects positioning rather than real demand, so it's vulnerable to a bounce. If we can get a resolution in the war, I think we can get below $80 and it should stick around the $80-85 level as inventories are rebuilt.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Bitcoin is doing it's ABCs technically. What will the buyers and selllers do at the old support?
item.description:
Bitcoin is doing its ABCs technically. The A leg was Thursday’s sharp break lower, the B leg was the corrective bounce over the weekend, and the C leg took the price through Friday’s floor and toward the 200-day moving average. Buyers have stepped in ahead of that moving average twice. The next test is whether they can get the price back above the old floor.

In the video above, I walk through each leg of the move and look at what buyers need to do to take back some control, where sellers can lean against the bounce, and what comes into play if the 200-day moving average gives way.

A. The risk-off move breaks the hourly moving averages.

On Thursday, Bitcoin came under pressure as risk-off flows picked up in the aftermath of the US election. The price fell below both the 100- and 200-hour moving averages with momentum and stayed below them. That was the first technical clue that sellers had taken control.

The swing-area floor near $74,925 held on Friday. Buyers had a level to lean against, and the hold gave them room to push the price back up over the weekend. The next question was what would happen when that bounce ran into resistance.

B. The weekend correction stalls at the broken 38.2% retracement.

The bounce carried Bitcoin back toward the broken 38.2% retracement at $76,052. Sellers leaned against it, and the price rotated back to the downside. That gave traders a level to define risk on the topside and put Friday’s floor back in focus.

This time, the floor near $74,925 gave way. With buyers losing the level they had defended on Friday, the price stretched toward the next major target, the 200-day moving average.

C. Buyers lean ahead of the 200-day moving average.

The low reached $73,460, about $310 above the 200-day MA at $73,153. Today, the price came within about $500 of the moving average before bouncing again. Buyers are stepping in ahead of it, and the moving average is now the downside barometer for both sides.

On the topside, the old floor near $74,925 is close resistance. Getting back above it and holding would give buyers some added confidence and put the $76,052 retracement back in play. If sellers can keep a lid on the bounce near the old floor, they keep the near-term advantage. A break below the 200-day MA would give them more control and bring the 50% retracement at $72,554 into focus.

Education. How to use an ABC move to define risk.

In this example, the A leg established the downside bias when Bitcoin broke the hourly moving averages. The B leg showed where sellers were willing to step back in. The C leg then took out the prior low and brought the next support target into view. Each leg gave traders a level they could use to judge whether the price action was following through.

The next clue comes from how price behaves at the old floor. If Bitcoin gets above $74,925 and buyers defend it on a retest, they have a closer level to lean against and a reason to look toward $76,052. If the bounce stalls at the old floor, sellers have a nearby level to define their risk and the 200-day MA remains the target below. That’s how the same chart can give both sides a roadmap.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Morning Kickstart. Stock futures climb as Bitcoin nears its 200-day moving average. USD/oil lower.
item.description:

I use that number to judge how much ground it has already covered before deciding where I can define risk.

Bitcoin approaches its 200-day moving average

Bitcoin traded down to $73,650, its lowest level since August 21, before bouncing to around $74,821. The low was just $497 above the 200-day moving average at $73,153. August 21 was also the last time Bitcoin traded below that moving average.

The first downside target is back at $73,650. A break would put the 200-day moving average in play. That’s the bigger barometer for buyers and sellers. If the price tests the average and bounces, buyers have a level to lean against with risk defined. A break that holds below it would give sellers more control. If the price breaks below and quickly gets back above, I’ll be watching for a failed break.

Binance is also in focus. The exchange said Saturday that CFO Kaiser Ng is leaving to pursue another venture and that Justin Yek, formerly of Airwallex, will take over. Co-CEO Yi He said the transition had been in the works for six months. The announcement followed the October 29 theft of about $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency. Binance said the attackers compromised employee computers through malicious downloads and fake recruiting efforts targeting engineers, and the exchange pledged to reimburse affected customers in full. The FBI attributed the theft to a North Korean group. Pyongyang denied involvement.

The breach puts Binance’s security controls and its handling of reimbursements in focus. For Bitcoin, the immediate question is whether buyers can defend the August low and the 200-day moving average if the price rolls over again.

item.title: Gold futures rallied $81, then gave back $51. Can buyers reclaim $4,115?
item.description:
Gold buyers stepped in after an overnight reversal, but the recovery is less convincing than the initial rebound suggests

A closer look at trading activity reveals why $4,115.50 is the next hurdle, while $4,092.30 remains the key downside test.

Gold futures started the week with an impressive rally followed by an equally important warning. After climbing from $4,062.50 to $4,143.30, December COMEX gold futures retreated $51 to $4,092.30. Buyers responded, but the evidence suggests they have not yet regained control of the short-term market.

Analysis snapshot: November 9, 2026, at 05:02 EST (10:02 UTC). December 2026 gold futures (GC) last traded at $4,107.90 in the supplied snapshot. This is not a live quote.

Gold's buyers returned, but something changed

Gold's overnight action presents an interesting contrast.

During Sunday's initial recovery, buying activity translated into meaningful upward price movement. In one hourly period, futures advanced from $4,064 to $4,113.20, supported by positive net aggressive buying.

That was constructive. Buyers were not simply active; they were moving the market.

Several hours later, however, the relationship between trading activity and price began to deteriorate.

One hourly period saw gold decline approximately $16 despite an almost neutral balance between aggressive buying and selling. The next period pushed the market down to $4,092.30 before buyers returned.

This suggests the earlier rally had lost some of its effectiveness.

Perhaps even more interesting was what followed.

Between approximately 03:35 and 05:00 EST, cumulative volume delta, which measures the running difference between aggressive buying and selling, improved from +213 to +437 contracts.

Yet gold's price barely responded, moving from $4,106.30 to $4,105.90 over the same comparison.

In other words, more aggressive buying was not producing sustained higher prices.

This does not prove that large sellers were deliberately absorbing demand. But it raises a reasonable question about how much buying strength remains beneath the surface.

For traders, the lesson is important: buying pressure alone is not sufficient evidence of a bullish reversal. Price also needs to advance and retain those gains.

The $4,115 area is where buyers need to prove themselves

The immediate technical picture remains mixed, with a slightly vulnerable short-term structure.

The broader recovery from Friday's lows has not been invalidated. But Sunday's rejection from $4,143.30 means buyers have work to do before another serious challenge of that high becomes more credible.

Here are the price areas that matter.

$4,104.60-$4,108.50: Immediate decision area

This was the market's vicinity at the analytical cutoff. A completed five-minute move above $4,108.50, followed by the ability to remain above it, would be an early sign of improvement.

$4,115.50-$4,119.70: First meaningful resistance

This is the more important recovery test. Sustained trade above this area would help repair the overnight breakdown and improve the case for further upside.

$4,123.20 and approximately $4,132: Next bullish checkpoints

These become more relevant if buyers reclaim the first resistance area. The $4,132 reference is approximate, not an exact execution trigger.

Beyond them, $4,143.30 is the overnight high, while $4,155.80 marks the larger November 5 swing high.

$4,098-$4,092.30: Critical downside support

This is the area buyers defended during the overnight correction. A sustained move below $4,092.30 would weaken the short-term recovery thesis and put lower historical reference prices back into focus.

Two scenarios for gold futures traders

Bullish scenario: Reclaim $4,115 and hold it

The first constructive signal would be a completed move above $4,108.50 that holds rather than immediately reversing.

A stronger bullish development would be sustained acceptance above $4,115.50, preferably followed by a successful retest.

If renewed aggressive buying also produces higher prices that hold, the recovery could extend toward $4,123.20 and approximately $4,132.

A subsequent challenge of $4,143.30 would become more credible if those intermediate areas are overcome.

However, renewed weakness below $4,104.60-$4,098 would challenge the immediate repair, while a sustained loss of $4,092.30 would be a more serious warning.

Bearish scenario: A break below $4,092.30

If gold falls below $4,092.30 and cannot recover that level, sellers would gain a stronger technical argument.

The first historical downside reference would be $4,079.50, followed by $4,062.50.

The important distinction is between briefly trading below support and establishing acceptance beneath it.

A temporary break followed by an immediate recovery is not the same thing as a confirmed bearish continuation.

If gold instead recovers above $4,104.60-$4,108.50 and holds, the immediate breakdown interpretation would weaken.

A third scenario: Gold simply remains in balance

Traders should also consider the possibility of gold continuing to fluctuate between approximately $4,098 and $4,115.50 without establishing direction.

Repeated reversals, alternating buying and selling pressure, and limited price progress would favor patience over aggressive entries.

Not every market movement creates an attractive trade.

For futures and prop traders, direction is only half the decision

Gold provides a useful example of why identifying the likely market direction is not the same as finding an attractive entry.

Consider a strictly hypothetical short position at $4,091 after a confirmed breakdown, with a stop at $4,108.50.

One Micro Gold futures contract (MGC) represents 10 troy ounces, meaning every $1 movement in gold equals $10 per contract.

That would produce the following illustrative risk profile:

  • Initial risk: $175 per Micro Gold contract, before costs.

  • First reference at $4,079.50: $115 potential gross profit, or approximately 0.66 times the initial risk.

  • Second reference at $4,062.50: $285 potential gross profit, or approximately 1.63 times the initial risk.

The first reference offers less potential reward than the initial risk.

That does not make every trade using this setup unsuitable. But it highlights why chasing a breakdown can become unattractive even when the directional assessment is reasonable.

For traders operating under funded-account or evaluation rules, the remaining permitted loss buffer, transaction costs, slippage and any applicable news restrictions are additional considerations. The terms depend on the specific program.

For further context, see our guide to trading on margin and understanding leverage.

US inflation data could provide the next catalyst

Technical levels will not be the only consideration this week.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics calendar schedules two important inflation reports:

  • Tuesday, November 10: October Consumer Price Index (CPI), 08:30 EST.

  • Friday, November 13: October Producer Price Index (PPI), 08:30 EST.

Inflation surprises can influence Treasury yields, the US dollar and expectations for Federal Reserve policy, all of which can affect gold.

A stronger-than-expected inflation reading could increase pressure on gold if it drives yields and the dollar higher. A softer reading could support the opposite response.

Neither relationship is guaranteed. The market's interpretation of the data and the resulting price action will matter.

These releases also introduce additional execution risk for short-term traders.

The bottom line for gold

Gold's overnight reversal does not eliminate the broader recovery, but it does expose a weakness that traders should not overlook.

Buyers successfully responded near $4,092.30, yet subsequent aggressive buying produced limited sustained upward progress.

My interpretation is that the market remains balanced, with some short-term downside vulnerability, until buyers demonstrate that they can reclaim and hold above $4,115.50.

A sustained break beneath $4,092.30 would change that assessment in favor of sellers.

Until one side provides stronger confirmation, the most valuable trading decision may be to wait.

Educational only. Trade at your own risk.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: Eurozone Sentix investor confidence weakens further in November as global growth momentum fades
item.description:
• Sentix index 2.4 vs 2.1 expected
  • Prior 2.7
  • Full report 

The Eurozone Sentix Investor Confidence Index edged lower in November, falling by 0.3 points to 2.4, as economic expectations continued to deteriorate. Investors are increasingly concerned about the sustainability of the recovery amid multiple headwinds.

The current situation component remained unchanged at -3.3, while the expectations index declined for the second consecutive month to 8.3, its lowest level since June 2026. Despite the slightly positive headline reading, the persistently negative assessment of current conditions says that the Eurozone economy remains stuck in a stagnation scenario.

The most notable deterioration in confidence came from the US, where the Sentix Economic Index fell by 2.0 points to 13.1, reaching its lowest level since June 2026. The decline was driven mainly by weakening expectations, which dropped by 3.5 points to -2.5, entering negative territory for the first time since June. In contrast, the current situation component remained relatively strong at 30.0.

Sentix highlighted concerns that a Democratic majority in both chambers of Congress could complicate Trump's economic agenda and limit the scope for additional fiscal stimulus. High financing costs and geopolitical risks are also contributing to growing uncertainty. 

The deterioration in sentiment is not limited to the US and Europe. The Sentix Global Aggregate Index declined for the third consecutive month, falling to 12.7, its lowest level since June 2026. Economic expectations weakened for the third month running to 9.3, while the assessment of current conditions remained relatively stable at 16.2.

On a more positive note, investors are anticipating some stabilisation in the inflation outlook. The Sentix inflation theme barometer improved from -29.25 to -22.5, while the central bank policy barometer rose from -21 to -12.75, suggesting expectations of a somewhat less restrictive monetary policy environment, although this comes with a worse growth outlook.

The Sentix survey points to a gradual deterioration in global economic expectations amid Democratic Congress, US-Iran war and central bank tightening. While current economic conditions remain resilient, investors are getting more and more concerned about the future outlook. 

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: Market outlook for the week of 9th - 13th November
item.description:
This week will have a slow start, with the only notable events for Monday being scheduled speeches from a few FOMC members.

On Tuesday, we'll get the Westpac consumer sentiment index in Australia, while the Bank of Japan and the Bank of Canada will release their respective meeting minutes. However, the most awaited release will be the inflation print in the U.S.

As a reminder, the BoJ kept rates unchanged at 1.25% at its last meeting, so traders will look for any hints in the Bank's Summary of Opinions about the possibility and timing of future rate hikes, as well as policymakers’ views on the progress of inflation.

Similarly, the BoC's Summary of Deliberations will provide more information about the Bank’s latest decision to raise rates. Arguments included higher energy costs and the resulting price pressures in the economy, while counter-arguments for holding rates were weaker economic growth and uncertainty surrounding U.S. tariffs. The focus will be on any clues about further tightening, but the Bank has signaled a cautious approach amid uncertainty.

Wednesday's economic calendar looks uneventful with both Canada and the U.S. observing bank holidays, while Thursday the focus will be on the U.K.'s GDP data.

The week will end with the PPI m/m release in the U.S., but it's worth noting that several FOMC members are expected to deliver remarks throughout the week.

In the U.S., the consensus for core CPI m/m is 0.2% vs. the prior 0.3%, while headline CPI m/m is expected at 0.3% vs. the prior 0.6%.

This CPI release will be somewhat different, as the BLS will not publish the year-on-year readings due to missing data from the October 2025 government shutdown. This puts the focus on the monthly figures.

Headline CPI is expected to rise by 0.28%, with slower gasoline inflation partly offset by higher food costs as increased commodity and transportation expenses feed through to consumers.

Core CPI is also likely to rise, but at a slower pace. Wells Fargo analysts expect goods inflation to ease, especially since the previous price increases in clothing and toys are unlikely to be repeated. Within services, shelter inflation is expected to return to a more normal pace, while travel-related costs should lose some momentum following previous increases in airfare and hotel prices.

A softer core inflation reading will signal some relief following last month’s upside surprise but the overall disinflation process remains slow and uneven, strengthening the case for another rate hike at the December meeting, Wells Fargo said. Meanwhile, Scotiabank analysts note that alternative data sources, including Bloomberg's price project, reinforce a recent rise in headline inflation year-over-year.

The U.S. will also release the PPI figures on Friday, but the annual reading faces the same limits as the CPI one due to missing data. The month-over-month print is expected at 0.4% vs. 1.3% prior.

In the U.K., the consensus for GDP m/m is 0.0% vs. the prior 0.1%, while preliminary GDP q/q is expected at 0.7% vs. the prior 0.5%. The main factors supporting growth have been business services and investment spending, particularly in activities related to AI and technology.

That said, higher energy bills and mortgage costs have continued to weigh on household spending and consumer-facing sectors. Survey data suggests that growth momentum weakened towards the end of the quarter, Wells Fargo analysts said. In terms of monetary policy, the BoE faces a challenging balancing act. Inflation remains a concern, while resilient economic activity gives policymakers less room to delay further tightening. As a reminder, the BoE delivered a 25 bps rate hike at its last meeting with another hike expected in Q1 next year.

This article was written by Gina Constantin at investinglive.com.

What are FX option expiries?

The FX option expiration price levels refer to the strike prices where option contracts are set to expire. These levels include both calls and puts.

When you see "EUR/USD at 1.1600 for €4 billion" it means there is a total of €4 billion worth of options (calls + puts combined) that have a strike price of 1.1600 and are expiring at that specific time (the "New York Cut" at 10:00 AM ET).

Traders watch these levels because they often act as a "magnet" for the price. For example, if there's nothing happening in the market and the price is close to the expiry level, let's say 30-50 pips away, what you will usually see is the price moving into the expiry level. This happens due to the hedging activity of the market makers (banks, dealers and so on).

As the price gets closer to the strike price near expiration, these market makers must aggressively buy or sell the currency to hedge their risk. This hedging activity tends to suppress volatility and keep the price "pinned" close to the strike price until the expiration time passes.
